stories.headline: Trumbull Restaurant Week returns Oct. 2–9 with 20 local eateries
stories.summary: Trumbull Restaurant Week runs October 2–9, inviting residents to support local restaurants with specials across roughly 20 participating spots, from Prime One Eleven and Izumi Sushi to Ecco Wine Bar, Fryborg, and Trumbull Pizza Company. Town officials call it a chance to back the business community while sampling limited-time menus. Full participant details are listed on the Trumbull Restaurant Week site and the town’s Patch wrap.

stories.headline: White House pushes faster DHS review of 47 state voter rolls for noncitizens
stories.summary: An internal DHS email seen by Reuters shows the White House pressing agencies to accelerate checks of at least 47 state voter rolls under an Unlawful Voter Initiative ahead of the midterms. Hundreds of officers have been surged, and rolls are being “enriched” with commercial Accurint data, raising false-positive risks for citizens. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said 1,620 cases are under investigation; Nevada previously saw a preliminary 16,000-name list shrink to 185 verified matches.

stories.headline: Trump admin releases CISA blueprint to harden 2026 election infrastructure
stories.summary: DHS and CISA released a 13-page 2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan outlining cyber and physical threats and free tools for election officials, including risk assessments, vulnerability scanning, regional advisors, and fusion-center intelligence sharing. The plan encourages paper ballots and post-election manual audits. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin framed election security as national security; the document marks a shift for an agency previously criticized for speech-policing roles.

stories.headline: Apple confirms iPhone 18 Pro Face ID fix update coming early next week
stories.summary: Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update early next week will address a Face ID bug affecting some iPhone 18 Pro users. The fix is expected to arrive as iOS 27.0.1, which Apple was already observed testing. The confirmation elevates yesterday’s build-watch into an official timeline for owners who have seen Face ID fail to unlock or authorize apps.

stories.headline: Qualcomm renews global patent licensing deal with Apple from April 2027
stories.summary: Qualcomm announced renewal of its global patent licensing agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027, without disclosing the new term length. The patent deal is separate from modem supply; Apple continues shifting to its own C2 modem, with only the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max still shipping a Qualcomm modem. The original post-settlement license began in 2019 and had been extended through March 2027.

stories.headline: Tesla Semi factory sneak peek: PepsiCo, DHL, US Foods trucks staged for tonight
stories.summary: Drone footage over Tesla’s new Nevada Semi plant shows at least 11 customer-branded Semis lined up ahead of tonight’s Rollout livestream (9 p.m. ET), including PepsiCo, US Foods, DHL, ArcBest/ABF, Einride, IMC, WattEV, and OK Produce. Familiar fleet names sit beside likely new order reveals. The dedicated factory, producing since April, is rated for 50,000 trucks a year; analysts still expect far fewer deliveries in 2026.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14 stacked at Starbase for first orbital attempt as early as Sep 28
stories.summary: SpaceX stacked Ship 41 on Super Heavy booster B21 at Starbase, assembling the 124-meter stack for Flight 14 — Starship’s first full orbital attempt. A window opens 7:15 a.m. CDT September 28 pending an FAA flight license; a temporary flight restriction runs through October 7. The planned ~10-hour mission would carry Starlink V3 satellites and attempt a Pacific splashdown west of Chile after six orbits.

stories.headline: Penguins 2026-27 preview: Crosby-era core still the foundation as youth push
stories.summary: NHL.com’s season preview frames Pittsburgh’s challenge as balancing contention with development around Crosby, Malkin, Karlsson, and Letang after last year’s playoff return. Goaltending (Silovs projected to start; Murashov as the upside backup), Andrei Kuzmenko’s one-year deal, and Nicholas Robertson’s Crosby-line looks are key watch items. Rutger McGroarty, Ville Koivunen, and Harrison Brunicke remain the youth bets as the regular season opens September 29.

stories.headline: Jets defense ranks No. 1 overall as Bailey and Thomas fuel Lions-week prep
stories.summary: Through two games the Jets sit No. 1 in total defense (197 yards allowed per game), No. 2 against the pass and run, while preparing for Sunday’s trip to Detroit. Second-year CB Azareye’h Thomas owns the NFL’s longest active pass-defensed streak, and rookie edge David Bailey already has two sacks. Safeties Andre Cisco and Dane Belton have covered for injured Minkah Fitzpatrick as Aaron Glenn’s unit emphasizes attacking the ball.

stories.headline: LEGO UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer: 6,130 pieces, $799.99, on sale Oct. 1
stories.summary: The LEGO Group’s Ultimate Collector Series Executor Super Star Destroyer (75457) is the longest LEGO Star Wars model yet at 6,130 pieces and 53.5 inches, priced at $799.99 and available October 1. It includes Darth Vader plus all six bounty hunters in one set for the first time, a minifig-scale bridge scene, a companion Star Destroyer, and a built-in stand. Early buyers (Oct. 1–7) get a Gift with Purchase Darth Vader Lightsaber set while stocks last.

stories.headline: Andrew Wilson drops Erika Kirk texts and video — Candace Owens still unconvinced
stories.summary: Commentator Andrew Wilson released private texts attributed to Erika Kirk and a September 8, 2025 video of Charlie Kirk with his daughter watching the Bears, arguing the family was home that evening. Critics note Erika does not appear in the clip, and Candace Owens continues to challenge metadata and timing. The fresh drop keeps the anniversary-cycle dispute over Erika’s whereabouts alive without settling the underlying questions.

stories.headline: Maine foliage report: northern color change high as nor’easter threatens weekend
stories.summary: Maine’s Thursday foliage report shows high color change in the north, moderate in central Maine, and still-low color in the south, where peak usually arrives mid-to-late October. Drought is accelerating progression and may shorten the season, spokesperson Gale Ross warned, while urging leaf-peepers to watch a rare September nor’easter forecast for the weekend coast. Northern peak traditionally lands the last week of September through the first week of October.
